Executive Summary

CareConnect is a role-based digital platform designed to support home-based palliative care for patients with advanced cancer. The application brings patients, nurses, doctors, and administrators into one coordinated care environment where health information, symptom monitoring, medication use, appointments, alerts, communication, and care planning can be followed in a structured way.

The project was developed to address a common challenge in palliative care: patients often receive support across several people and settings, yet the information needed to guide care may be fragmented. By organizing patient data and care activities in one place, CareConnect helps improve continuity, reduce delays in response, and support more timely clinical decisions.

The main beneficiaries are patients living with advanced illness, nurses who provide day-to-day monitoring and follow-up, doctors who make care decisions and adjust treatment, and administrators who oversee service coordination and patient assignment. The application is especially valuable in home-based palliative care because it supports comfort, symptom control, medication adherence, and rapid escalation when urgent attention is needed.

Introduction

Advanced cancer is often accompanied by pain, fatigue, breathlessness, anxiety, reduced appetite, and other distressing symptoms that affect daily life and family wellbeing. Home-based palliative care is important because many patients prefer to remain at home while still receiving organized support from a healthcare team.

Digital healthcare solutions can strengthen this model by making patient status visible to the care team, supporting timely communication, and helping staff respond to changes in symptoms or risk. A well-designed digital system can also reduce paperwork, improve record consistency, and make it easier to follow each patient across time.

The purpose of CareConnect is to support this coordinated care model. The application helps patients report symptoms and medication use, allows nurses and doctors to monitor care needs, and gives administrators a clearer overview of service activity. In practical terms, it promotes safer, more responsive, and more organized palliative care at home.

System Overview

CareConnect is organized around four main user groups: patient, nurse, doctor, and administrator. Each group sees a workspace that matches its responsibilities and the type of information it needs.

The system supports patient care by bringing together vital signs, medication tracking, symptom check-ins, emergency escalation, appointments, communication threads, care plans, and follow-up reporting. It supports healthcare management by making assignments visible, highlighting active alerts, and giving leadership a summary view of clinical activity and service workload.

User Roles

Patient

The patient role is focused on self-reporting and daily participation in care. Patients can review their health status, record symptoms, follow medication schedules, view upcoming appointments, communicate with assigned staff, and activate urgent help when necessary.

Benefits: greater reassurance, easier self-management, clearer understanding of care plans, and faster access to support.

Nurse

The nurse role supports continuous monitoring and practical follow-up. Nurses can review assigned patients, evaluate alert levels, respond to concerns, document visits, add communication notes, and coordinate care actions that support symptom control and comfort.

Benefits: better visibility into patient status, more efficient prioritization, and stronger continuity of home care.

Doctor

The doctor role focuses on clinical oversight, treatment decisions, care planning, prescriptions, and appointment management. Doctors review patient histories, assess progress, adjust care plans, and record outcomes that inform the next stage of care.

Benefits: clearer decision-making, improved coordination with nurses, and a more complete view of patient progress over time.

Administrator

The administrator role oversees users, assignments, program analytics, and service-level monitoring. This role helps ensure that care teams are properly organized and that operational decisions can be guided by system-wide information.

Benefits: improved service governance, better workload distribution, and stronger oversight of care delivery.

Detailed Feature Analysis

1. Authentication and Login

Purpose: To protect patient information and make sure each person sees only the information that matches their role.

User experience: Users sign in and are taken to a role-specific workspace.

Benefits: safer access, confidential handling of health data, and an organized entry point for care activities.

2. Patient Overview Dashboard

Purpose: To present a snapshot of current health indicators and active items relevant to the patient.

User experience: The patient sees blood pressure, blood sugar, heart rate, oxygen levels, medication status, upcoming items, and an emergency link.

Benefits: helps patients stay aware of their condition and supports early recognition of change.

3. Vital Signs Monitoring

Purpose: To track trends in blood pressure and related health indicators over time.

User experience: Patients and clinicians can review current readings and trends in a chart format.

Benefits: supports early identification of deterioration and improves continuity between home observations and clinical review.

4. Medication Tracking

Purpose: To support adherence to prescribed medicines and keep the patient aware of due doses.

User experience: The patient can view medication names, dose information, next dose timing, adherence status, and mark doses as taken.

Benefits: improves adherence, reduces missed doses, and gives nurses and doctors a clearer picture of treatment use.

5. Emergency Escalation

Purpose: To provide a rapid route for urgent assistance when the patient feels unsafe or severely unwell.

User experience: The patient follows a simple emergency pathway and receives confirmation that the alert has been sent.

Benefits: shortens response time, reduces anxiety, and helps the care team prioritize urgent situations.

6. Patient-to-Nurse and Patient-to-Doctor Communication

Purpose: To keep communication open between the patient and the assigned care team.

User experience: The patient can use conversation threads to send messages to the nurse or doctor and follow replies.

Benefits: improves reassurance, reduces unnecessary visits, and supports timely advice without waiting for the next appointment.

7. Palliative Symptom Check-In

Purpose: To collect information about symptom burden in a structured way.

User experience: The patient reports symptoms such as pain, nausea, fatigue, appetite change, or emotional distress.

Benefits: gives the team a clearer basis for comfort-focused care and supports earlier intervention when symptoms worsen.

8. Nurse Alert Triage

Purpose: To help nurses identify which patient issues need attention first.

User experience: Nurses review active alerts, evaluate urgency, and resolve concerns when appropriate.

Benefits: reduces missed warning signs and improves response to symptom deterioration.

9. Nurse Patients List

Purpose: To show the nurse the assigned patients, their conditions, risk level, and adherence status.

User experience: The nurse can scan the list and quickly decide who needs follow-up first.

Benefits: supports prioritization and efficient home-care scheduling.

10. Nurse Visit Logging

Purpose: To record home visits and clinical interactions.

User experience: The nurse schedules visits, adds observations, and documents communication notes.

Benefits: improves continuity, strengthens handover, and preserves a clinical record of care delivered at home.

11. Doctor Patients Review

Purpose: To allow doctors to review the patients under their care and the main concerns affecting them.

User experience: The doctor sees assigned patients, risk patterns, and key health information in one place.

Benefits: supports targeted clinical decisions and better oversight of complex cases.

12. Appointment Management

Purpose: To organize and review upcoming appointments and visits.

User experience: Doctors can view planned appointments and arrange care-related follow-up.

Benefits: improves planning, reduces missed follow-up, and helps align clinical review with patient needs.

13. Prescription Review and Renewal

Purpose: To support ongoing medication management for palliative patients.

User experience: Doctors can renew treatment-related items and review medication-related needs.

Benefits: helps maintain continuity of therapy and supports symptom relief through timely adjustments.

14. Palliative Care Plan Review

Purpose: To guide individualized symptom relief and comfort-oriented care.

User experience: Doctors can review and update care priorities, goals, and the patient’s current needs.

Benefits: promotes goal-directed care, strengthens patient-centered planning, and supports family understanding.

15. Outcome Recording

Purpose: To capture the patient’s overall response to palliative care.

User experience: Clinicians enter outcome information that reflects physical, emotional, social, or spiritual progress.

Benefits: shows whether the care plan is helping and supports evidence-informed adjustment.

16. Administrator User Management

Purpose: To oversee the user directory and ensure that the right people are active in the system.

User experience: Administrators review patient and staff records and manage the user base.

Benefits: maintains safe access and supports accurate organizational records.

17. Assignment Management

Purpose: To connect patients with the appropriate nurse and doctor.

User experience: Administrators allocate patients to staff and review care-team ownership.

Benefits: improves continuity of care, clarifies responsibility, and avoids confusion about who should respond.

18. Analytics and Oversight

Purpose: To provide a summary view of activity, risk, adherence, and service patterns.

User experience: Administrators can review charts and summary indicators from the platform.

Benefits: supports quality improvement, workload awareness, and program evaluation.

19. Notification Feed and Preferences

Purpose: To keep users informed of important events and allow them to manage how they receive updates.

User experience: Users can review recent notifications and adjust preferences.

Benefits: improves response to urgent events and respects communication needs.

User Workflows

Patient Journey

  1. The patient signs in and enters the personal workspace.
  2. The patient reviews current health indicators, medication status, and upcoming items.
  3. The patient records symptom information or completes a check-in when feeling unwell.
  4. The patient reads the care plan and follows the medication schedule.
  5. The patient communicates with the nurse or doctor if advice or reassurance is needed.
  6. If the situation becomes urgent, the patient activates the emergency pathway so the team can respond quickly.

Nurse Workflow

  1. The nurse signs in and reviews assigned patients.
  2. The nurse checks active alerts and identifies high-risk concerns.
  3. The nurse reviews symptom reports, adherence patterns, and messages from patients.
  4. The nurse documents visits, adds communication notes, and follows up on unresolved issues.
  5. The nurse escalates concerns to the doctor when a clinical decision is needed.

Doctor Workflow

  1. The doctor signs in and opens the clinician workspace.
  2. The doctor reviews the assigned patient list, appointments, and symptom trends.
  3. The doctor examines the patient’s palliative status, medication needs, and care plan.
  4. The doctor adjusts treatment, renews prescriptions when appropriate, and records outcomes.
  5. The doctor coordinates with the nurse to align home follow-up and symptom response.

Administrator Workflow

  1. The administrator signs in and opens the oversight dashboard.
  2. The administrator reviews users, assignments, and service summaries.
  3. The administrator checks alerts and platform activity to identify operational concerns.
  4. The administrator updates assignments or user records when staffing changes occur.
  5. The administrator uses analytics to monitor workload, adherence, and overall program performance.

Benefits of the System

Benefits for Patients

  • Greater sense of safety through easy access to the care team.
  • Better understanding of medications, symptoms, and upcoming care actions.
  • Faster communication when symptoms worsen.
  • Improved support for staying at home rather than repeatedly attending hospital.
  • More active participation in care decisions and self-monitoring.

Benefits for Nurses

  • Clearer view of assigned patients and their risk profile.
  • Faster prioritization of urgent concerns.
  • Better documentation of visits and communication.
  • Improved coordination with doctors and patients.
  • Support for evidence-based symptom management in the home setting.

Benefits for Doctors

  • More complete picture of patient progress between visits.
  • Better ability to adjust treatment according to symptom trends.
  • Improved review of care plans, prescriptions, and outcomes.
  • More efficient collaboration with nurses.
  • Stronger follow-up of advanced cancer care priorities.

Benefits for Healthcare Organizations

  • More organized assignment and oversight of staff workload.
  • Improved consistency in patient records and care coordination.
  • Potential reduction in avoidable admissions through earlier intervention.
  • Better visibility into service activity and palliative program performance.
  • Support for quality improvement and academic evaluation of care outcomes.

Healthcare Impact

CareConnect can improve patient outcomes by helping the care team notice changes sooner and respond in a more organized manner. In palliative care, small delays can lead to unnecessary suffering; a shared digital view helps reduce that risk.

Communication is strengthened because the patient, nurse, and doctor can all work from the same care context. This reduces the chance that an important message is missed or repeated, and it allows care decisions to be based on more current information.

Care coordination also improves because responsibilities are clearer. The nurse knows which patients need attention, the doctor knows where clinical decisions are required, and the administrator can monitor the overall structure of care delivery.

Administrative burden is reduced because routine information is organized in one place instead of being scattered across separate notes or informal communication. This is especially valuable in home-based care where follow-up often depends on timely documentation.

The system supports evidence-based nursing practice by encouraging structured symptom review, documented follow-up, and consistent attention to patient response over time. That makes it easier to evaluate whether interventions are helping and whether the care plan should be adjusted.

Future Enhancements

  • Expanded patient education modules tailored to symptom patterns and treatment stages.
  • More detailed care-plan version history for long-term clinical review.
  • Stronger appointment scheduling with reminders and conflict checks.
  • More advanced quality indicators for program evaluation.
  • Additional family or caregiver participation features where appropriate.
  • Offline-friendly support for low-connectivity home-care settings.
  • Accessibility improvements for patients and staff with differing digital needs.

Conclusion

CareConnect was developed to support a structured home-based palliative care program for patients with advanced cancer. Its main objective is to improve symptom management, medication adherence, communication, care coordination, and oversight across the patient journey.

The key features of the system center on patient self-reporting, nursing follow-up, doctor-led clinical decision-making, and administrator oversight. Together, these functions create a more connected and responsive care environment.

From a healthcare perspective, the project demonstrates how a digital platform can strengthen palliative care delivered at home. It supports comfort, dignity, continuity, and timely response, all of which are important in the care of people living with advanced cancer.
